_comment: Contracts that are declared but have no producing code yet.
ADR-0002 makes contract-first a rule: a schema lands as its own reviewed change,
with a version bump, BEFORE any code implementing it. That rule collides with the
schema-coverage check in test/contract-conformance.test.ts, which requires every
schema on disk to be validated against a value the running system produced.
Both are right. This file is the seam between them: a schema listed here is
exempt from needing a produced value, and says why and what will produce it.
Two rules keep it from becoming a place schemas go to be forgotten, matching the
- an entry with no reason or no `produced_by` fails;
- an entry whose schema HAS a conformance case is stale and fails, so the
exemption cannot outlive the implementation it was waiting for.
Every entry below is ADR-0008 action item 1: the evaluation plane's contracts,
landing ahead of the pipeline that will emit them.

pending.reason: The versioned artifact. Nothing constructs one until the evaluation pipeline exists; until then the authoring pipeline works in terms of PipelineCommand, which carries a subset.
No suite exists yet. The smoke/anchor distinction is the reason this schema lands before the first suite is written, so the first suite has to declare which job it is doing.
Requires a failure_mode per case, which is a constraint on how the first suite is written and therefore has to exist before it.
Emitted by the evaluation pipeline's execute and aggregate steps, neither of which exists.
Emitted by the judge adapter. Landing it first is deliberate: it makes runs, disagreement_rate and position_randomized mandatory before anyone writes a judge that would otherwise omit them.
Written by the release pipeline when a run is promoted. No promotion path exists.
Emitted by the comparator. Landing it first fixes `inconclusive` and `refused` as real verdicts before an implementation can quietly reduce the outcome space to improved/regressed.
